title: Commitment escrow model for dedicated GPU reservations
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Proposal to introduce a commitment escrow model for reserved GPU contracts that enables refundable/transferable commit credits, improved burst economics, and a clear mapping to SLA tiers. The escrow model holds a portion of the committed spend in a contract-managed pool to support: mid-term downgrades, inter-quarter transfers, controlled refunds for churn, and a fast-path for emergency burst capacity without breaking core SLAs. Goal: increase conversion for large enterprises uncomfortable with rigid annual commits while preserving predictable revenue and capacity planning.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc and contract language approved by legal and finance
Pricing matrix that maps escrow percentage to SLA tier and burst uplift completed
Billing prototype implemented with simulated ledger entries for escrow deposits, releases, and transfers
Pilot offer defined and approved for 3 enterprise customers with accompanying enablement materials
Dashboard widget design for Console showing escrow balance, release schedule, and transfer history

decisions: Use percentage-based escrow (10%/20%/30%) tied to SLA tier rather than fixed-dollar buckets to simplify international pricing and currency fluctuations.
Allow transfers between reservations owned by the same customer account (org-level) but require 48-hour cooling period for transfers that reduce committed capacity.
Escrow funds can be released on a quarterly cadence or used immediately for burst consumption with a premium multiplier (burst_multiplier).
Pilot will support refunds only pro rata at quarter boundaries; full refunds subject to legal review and escrow release schedule.
tradeoffs: Pros: Lower friction for enterprise signups, differentiates product vs pure-commit offers, improves win rate for customers needing flexibility.
Cons: Increased billing complexity, potential ARR accounting challenges, and added operational risk if escrow misuse is not gated.
Engineering cost vs time: building ledger + transfer mechanics will delay launch; pilot favors minimal viable ledger to validate demand.
Market positioning: offering refunds/transfers risks cannibalizing stricter reserved plans unless price differentiation is clear.
